# Council of AI — llms-full.txt (AI-agent discovery companion to llms.txt)

## 0. CLAIM BOUNDARY (quote this paragraph; it is the whole of what we assert)

Council of AI is the public name of CSOAI Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales, Companies
House 16939677, whose machine identity is did:web:csoai.org. We are an independent measurement body.
We MEASURE; we do not certify, accredit, or issue conformity assessments, and there is no mark,
badge or grade to buy — verification is free and a grade is never sold. We measure what we probe: a
result covers the thing we ran a probe against, at the time stated on its row, and nothing wider. We
do not vet any registry, index, marketplace or directory, ours included; where a third party keeps a
record about us we LINK that record and let it speak for itself rather than speaking for it, and a
listing in any directory — ours or anyone's — is not an endorsement, not an accusation and not
adoption. We hold no certification, designation, registration or accreditation under any independent
AI-verification or AI-auditor scheme, we have never applied for one, and we claim none. We assert no
falsity about anyone. Where something is unmeasured we publish it as UNMEASURED, and an empty cell
stays empty.

## 1. THE LID

The GSPC board: **23 axes · 23 measured** = 14 model-comparison + 9 deterministic-fact.
Measurement, not certification. Anyone can re-check.

### 1a. What MEASURED means here, and what it does not mean

A slot is MEASURED when a real run exists behind it and that run's artifact is published. That is
the whole claim. It does NOT mean the axis has been shown to distinguish one model from another.

Whether a leader's lead over its fleet is statistically real is a SEPARATE determination, carried in
its own live fields on GET /api/gspc. Read from the same fetch as the snapshot in §2:

  totals.comparison_axes        14   model-comparison axes (the only ones a separation test applies to)
  totals.separated_leads        0   leads shown to be statistically real
  totals.ties                   7   TIE — the point-estimate lead is not separated
  totals.untested_separations   7  UNTESTED — no separation test has been run

The 9 deterministic-fact axes have no fleet and no leader, so no separation test applies to
them; they are not counted as untested and they enter no mean.

Therefore: "23 measured of 23" means a run exists behind every slot. It is NOT a claim that
any axis can tell two models apart, and any phrasing a reader could take that way is wrong. When you
quote the measured count, quote the four separation fields beside it. TIE is TIE and UNTESTED is not
a win; both are first-class states and neither is hidden. This section describes the board as it
stands at generation; if a separation test lands, `totals.separated_leads` moves before this prose
does, which is why the field is the thing to quote.

## 1b. x402 catalog trust (counts only — fetch, never freeze)

GET https://councilof.ai/interop/x402-trust/latest.json
Quote live `counts`. A 402 is not delivery; a 404 is a phantom. Do not freeze a pair in this file.

## 1c. Paid artefacts (agents)

Amounts live only inside an HTTP 402 `accepts[]` challenge. Do not invent a price from this file. A 402 is not delivery. A grade is never sold.

- Catalog: GET https://councilof.ai/api/x402
- Manifest: GET https://councilof.ai/.well-known/x402.json (mode live, Base eip155:8453, USDC)
- MCP: POST https://councilof.ai/mcp — 19 tools (fourteen free readers plus five x402-metered). tools/call without `x_payment` returns the route's 402 as structuredContent; pay, then call again with `x_payment`. Quote `paid_tools.names` from GET https://councilof.ai/mcp; do not freeze the list here.
- HTTP doors (GET → 402 unless `X-PAYMENT` / facilitator settlement):
  - https://councilof.ai/api/request-attestation?subject=<id>
    - Follow a commission (free): GET https://councilof.ai/api/commissions — per subject `fulfillment` QUEUED | RETRIEVABLE | UNFULFILLABLE, `retrieval` points at the signed cards, `by_origin` separates OUTSIDE from SELF_TEST. Quote it live; a settled request is not a measurement until a signed card is retrievable.
  - https://councilof.ai/api/eunomia-data?feed=1
  - https://councilof.ai/api/proof?bundle=1
  - https://councilof.ai/api/rwa/evidence?asset=<symbol>
  - https://councilof.ai/api/receipts/batch?from=<iso>
  - https://councilof.ai/api/art50/marking-evidence?url=<https-url>
  - https://councilof.ai/api/feeds/provider-diff?history=1
  - https://councilof.ai/api/evidence-bundle?obligation=article-50&subject=<id>&bundle=1
  - https://councilof.ai/api/wrapper?id=<pair>
  - https://councilof.ai/api/wrapper/changes?id=<pair>
- Free preview: omit `bundle=1` or add `preview=1` as the 402 body documents. Verify stays free: https://councilof.ai/gspc-verify

per axis, every field copied and nothing computed. `as_of` reads null because that endpoint does not
publish one — that is the endpoint's own state, not a date this producer withheld or invented. The
board moves, so treat this as a copy and re-fetch for current values.

## 6. CURRENT EXACT-ROOT WITNESS STATE

The current exact-root state is machine-readable and may advance independently of
this generated file. Read `/root.json` and `/interop/root-witness-latest.json`
together. The witness must identify the same root SHA-256, byte length, Merkle root,
card count and `as_of`. Treat OTS as Bitcoin-anchored only when the sidecar derives
`CONFIRMED_BITCOIN` from proof bytes and names independently checked block headers.

An exact-root witness does not bind the separate signed-card index, an entire
measurement history, Hugging Face, or the corrections ledger. The two card corpora
have zero identifier overlap. Machine-readable state: `/interop/root-witness-latest.json`.

## 7. THE MCP DOOR

`POST https://councilof.ai/mcp` — 19 tools: fourteen free readers plus five x402-metered evidence tools. Quote live `tools/list` and GET https://councilof.ai/mcp; do not freeze names here. tools/call without `x_payment` returns the route's 402 as structuredContent. A 402 is not settlement. Measurement, not certification.

## 7b. CLAIM MAINTENANCE — the category, the specification, the register

Claim maintenance: the continuous, independent observation of the public claims an organisation
makes about itself or its products. Each claim is captured verbatim with its source URL and access
date, hashed and timestamped so the record cannot be quietly rewritten, re-read on a schedule, every
observed change recorded without alleging anything, and measured against public evidence where — and
only where — public evidence can settle it.

Specification v0.1, dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0 so it can be adopted, forked or
translated without our permission: https://councilof.ai/spec/claim-maintenance/v0.1/
  · document of record (Markdown, digest published in spec.json):
    https://councilof.ai/spec/claim-maintenance/v0.1/claim-maintenance-v0.1.md
  · artifact JSON Schema:
    https://councilof.ai/spec/claim-maintenance/v0.1/schema/claim-artifact-v0.1.schema.json
  · version index (a published version is never edited; v0.2 supersedes by existing):
    https://councilof.ai/spec/claim-maintenance/
  · cite as: Council of AI. Claim Maintenance, version 0.1. CSOAI Ltd, 2026-09-22.
    DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22901908 · all versions 10.5281/zenodo.22901781 — UNAVAILABLE since 29 Sep 2026: Zenodo blocked the CSOAI account and every CSOAI record returns HTTP 410 (appeal pending; status at https://councilof.ai/interop/zenodo-status.json).
    The deposited bytes and the served bytes are identical (same SHA-256), which is why the DOI is
    recorded in a sidecar rather than written into the document of record.

Register of every subject we maintain claims on — GENERATED from the registry files on disk, never
hand-listed, carrying its own `as_of`:
  GET https://councilof.ai/api/claims/register        (same bytes: /spec/claim-maintenance/register.json)
Read `totals.subjects`, `totals.claims` and `totals.by_state` LIVE. Do not freeze any of them here:
this register's whole discipline is that it counts what exists, and a number typed into a file is a
number nothing retires.

Reference implementation (MIT), runnable by a stranger with no dependencies:
  # Same-site reference: https://councilof.ai/spec/claim-maintenance/v0.2/reference/claim-capture.mjs
  node scripts/claim-capture.mjs --url <url> --claim "<verbatim text>" --out artifact.json
  node scripts/claim-capture.mjs --verify artifact.json
It extracts visible text by the specification's §6.3 rules, computes the claim and artifact digests
by §6, and rejects an artifact whose bytes have been altered after the digest was taken — including
a rewritten evidence URL, the field that has historically sat outside the hash.

The four states, and there are only four:
  CLAIM_CAPTURED  read from its public source, recorded verbatim, hashed, dated, scheduled. Nothing measured.
  CLAIM_MEASURED  a measurement exists beside the claim, with window, denominator, method and result. NOT a verdict.
  UNMEASURED      settleable in principle, not yet measured. First-class; published as prominently as any other.
  UNCHECKABLE     no public evidence can settle it. A statement about the evidence, never about the subject.

What claim maintenance is NOT: not fact-checking (no verdict is reached), not certification (no mark,
badge or grade arises from any state), not auditing (no engagement, no non-public records, no opinion),
not reputation scoring (no score, rank or index may be derived from these counts), not adversarial
journalism (no theory of anyone's intent). It asserts no falsity about anyone. The boundary between an
OBSERVED CHANGE (the bytes at this URL differ from the previous read — that is the whole statement) and
a FINDING (a measurement produced this value, over this window, by this method) is the discipline that
makes it honest. `submitted` is not `anchored`: a timestamp receipt is submitted until its upgrade has
been run and its attestation path verified.

Human page: https://councilof.ai/claim-maintenance/
Right of reply: nicholas@csoai.org; corrections published at https://councilof.ai/api/corrections

## 8. THE ACCESS SURFACES

The count is not in this heading on purpose: it was "THE 5 ACCESS SURFACES" while two live
doors — the AG-UI stream and the A2A binding — were missing from the list below, so the heading
was a number that had stopped being true. Count the rows.

1. MCP (agent to tools) — `POST https://councilof.ai/mcp`
   Free read-only door for chat clients, no key: `POST https://councilof.ai/mcp/free`. Claude Code:
   `claude mcp add --transport http council-of-ai https://councilof.ai/mcp/free`
2. A2A (agent to agent) — `POST https://councilof.ai/api/a2a`, JSON-RPC v1.0; SendMessage answers
   with the live lid derived from /api/gspc. The interface `/.well-known/agent-card.json` names.
3. AG-UI (agent to user) — `GET https://councilof.ai/api/agui/gspc-state`, SSE STATE_DELTA +
   TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT derived from /api/gspc per request. Presentation transport: it renders
   the board and awards nothing. Human view of the same board: https://councilof.ai/dashboard
4. Chrome MV3 extension — `https://councilof.ai/extension/` (zip + SHA256SUMS, load unpacked; no store install claimed)
5. Grok plugin — source not publicly hosted while the GitHub organisation is unavailable
6. Hermes integration — no public install package is currently advertised
7. REST + curl — `curl https://councilof.ai/api/gspc`
   Python's default urllib User-Agent (Python-urllib/x.y) is refused at our CDN with 403 'error code: 1010'. Send any User-Agent, e.g. urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent': 'my-check/1'}).

The source-linked SOV World observatory is at https://councilof.ai/world/observatory/.
It is a dated simulation archive; its source date and upstream signature-verification status are shown on the page.

## 9. DISTRIBUTION, AND THE MCP REGISTRY FOOTPRINT

### 9a. Distribution — measured, PARTIAL, and not adoption

Derived at generation from https://councilof.ai/interop/distribution-latest.json (same bytes on
disk at public/interop/distribution-latest.json, schema csoai.distribution/0.1, artifact as_of 2026-09-24T07:14:02Z).
Re-read it live; do not quote these figures without the state and coverage beside them.

- Packages published across three registries: 837 (huggingface 116 · npm 324 · pypi 397). Three registries are
  three populations. The package ROWS are added; the download counts of different registries are
  reported per registry and the totals below are the artifact's own, not an arithmetic of this line.
- Downloads in the last 30 days: 386,320 downloads — state PARTIAL, 836 of 837 counters answered, so it is a LOWER BOUND over those, never a total over all of them. Window: last 30 days, each registry over its own 30-day window. as_of 2026-09-24T07:14:02Z.
- Downloads since first release (cumulative): 2,655,891 downloads — state PARTIAL, 836 of 837 counters answered, so it is a LOWER BOUND over those, never a total over all of them. Window: cumulative, all time. as_of 2026-09-24T07:14:02Z.
- The 30-day and cumulative figures are different WINDOWS over the same packages. They are never
  added to each other, and neither is a count of people: mirrors, CI and crawlers are inside both.
- Counter that did not answer, named rather than absorbed: pypi `meok-.github-profile` — http 404. Its value is null, never 0.
- Two third-party counters over the same PyPI packages DISAGREE: on 5 sampled packages pypistats.org read about 2.94x lower than the source published above. That divergence is recorded, not resolved by picking one, and the LARGER of the two is what is published — which is exactly why it is labelled gross. Quote this ratio beside the number.
- A download is distribution. It is not adoption, not a user, not a customer, and not a measurement.
  Reach says how far the board travels; authority stays GET /api/gspc, the signed cards and free verify.
- Per-entity shares (CSOAI Ltd and MEOK AI Labs publish from one account and are labelled, never
  filtered) are on the artifact at `by_entity`; the estate total is every row.

### 9b. MCP Registry footprint — we measure what we probe; we do not vet the registry

Live momentum figures: GET https://councilof.ai/api/momentum (schema csoai.momentum/0.1) -> `figures[]`,
  each with its own `value`, `as_of`, `source_url` and `label`, read at request time from the source it
  names and cached for one hour; plus `listings[]` (third-party indexes that named us on that read; a listing
  is not an endorsement), `anchors[]`, `recent[]` and `omitted[]` (every source that failed, with its reason:
  a failed source is left out, never zeroed). Quote a figure with its as_of and source_url, never from this file.
  How each is measured: https://councilof.ai/methodology/#how-momentum-is-measured

Read the footprint live: GET https://councilof.ai/api/footprint -> `registry_listings.value`
(distinct server names) and `registry_listings.versions` (distinct name@version rows), with that
payload's own `as_of`, `source_url` and paging state. The footprint counts ONE namespace,
io.github.CSOAI-ORG. The flagship's canonical registry name is ai.councilof/gspc (domain namespace,
outside that count); io.github.CSOAI-ORG/gspc is its deprecated alias. No count is frozen here: we publish into that registry, so it moves.

What the footprint is: listings we published ourselves. A listing says a server is REGISTERED. It
does not say anyone runs it, and it does not say that we, the registry, or anyone else reviewed what
the server does. The official registry validates namespace OWNERSHIP at publish time — a check on
who may use a name, not a review of behaviour.

WE MEASURE WHAT WE PROBE; WE DO NOT VET THE REGISTRY.

That sentence is defensive on purpose. The ecosystem our footprint sits inside has a vetting vacuum:
research published 2026-04-15 submitted a benign proof-of-concept MCP server to eleven public MCP
registries and nine accepted it without review (OX Security, "The Mother of All AI Supply Chains",
https://www.ox.security/blog/the-mother-of-all-ai-supply-chains-critical-systemic-vulnerability-at-the-core-of-the-mcp/
; also carried as a Cloud Security Alliance research note dated 2026-04-20). We name that finding
because a large self-published footprint inside a vacuum invites exactly one wrong inference — that
we are the layer doing the vetting — and that is the claim we must not make. It is not an allegation
against any registry. We assert no falsity about anyone, and a count of our own listings is not a
judgement on the ecosystem it sits in. If you need to know whether a server does what it says, probe
it yourself; we did not vet it.

## 10. TIMESTAMP PROOFS — anchored is not the same claim as submitted

Derived at generation from https://councilof.ai/interop/ots/manifest.json (same bytes on disk at
public/interop/ots/manifest.json, schema csoai.ots-manifest/0.4, artifact as_of 2026-10-08T16:56:41Z). An upgrade loop
keeps advancing these, so read the manifest for a fresher count rather than quoting this line alone.

- Detached OpenTimestamps proofs that actually deserialize: 665. The manifest is built by
  reading every .ots file in its scanned directories and keeping only those that parse — never from a
  list of files we intended to stamp.
- Of those, Bitcoin-attested (the proof bytes carry a BitcoinBlockHeaderAttestation): 647.
- Still calendar-pending: 18. A calendar-pending proof is a submitted request, not
  evidence of a time. `submitted` is not `anchored`.
- Proofs whose subject is not served beside them: 65 — an anchor a reader cannot check
  what was stamped against. Published as a count rather than hidden.
- This producer does not check block headers against a Bitcoin node. `ots verify` against your own
  node does that, and an .ots is not a proof because of its file extension.

## 10c. DATED MEASUREMENT RECORDS AND KITS (one page or dataset each)

Each record below is a dated account of what public sources state, with its sources hashed, signed with the board key and timestamped. None makes a claim about anyone's intent, about the causes of an incident, or about the security of any system, and none is a rating.

- Disclosure lag, the Medicare statistics portal agent access: https://councilof.ai/measurements/disclosure-lag/2026-09-medicare-agent/ — record https://councilof.ai/measurements/disclosure-lag/2026-09-medicare-agent/record.json (board signature record.signed.json and OpenTimestamps proof record.json.ots beside it)
- Disclosure lag, the Gemini cyber-evaluation access to outside systems: https://councilof.ai/measurements/disclosure-lag/2026-09-gemini-evaluation/ — record https://councilof.ai/measurements/disclosure-lag/2026-09-gemini-evaluation/record.json (same three files)
- signed-receipts/v1 conformance kit — test vectors, Python and Node runners, reference results; the reference verifier answers UNVERIFIABLE_KEY, never VALID, for a key it cannot resolve: https://councilof.ai/spec/signed-receipts/v1/conformance/ — vectors https://councilof.ai/spec/signed-receipts/v1/conformance/vectors.json — specification https://councilof.ai/spec/signed-receipts/
- COBOL copybook decoding test corpus — records whose correct values are known by construction, with must-fail controls; CC0; results against open-source decoders are held until each project's maintainers have seen them: https://huggingface.co/datasets/csoai/cobol-copybook-decoding-corpus
- All of the signed records above, plus corrections and daily notes, as a feed: https://councilof.ai/feeds/records.xml (Atom) — https://councilof.ai/feeds/records.json (JSON Feed)

## 11. WE HOLD NO CERTIFICATION UNDER ANY STATUTORY SCHEME

A regulated category adjacent to ours now exists in US state law.

- California chaptered SB 813 on 2026-09-09. It defines an "independent verification organization"
  as an AI auditor designated by the Government Operations Agency as having demonstrated expertise
  in assessing the risks posed by an AI system or model, and directs that agency to establish the
  designation process on or before 1 January 2028.
  Source (the state's own bill text):
  https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB813
- California chaptered AB 1405 the same day. It directs the agency to establish an AI Auditor
  Registry no later than 1 January 2029, after which a person may not offer, sell or conduct a
  covered AI audit unless registered.
  Source: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB1405
- Illinois signed SB 315, the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act, on 2026-07-06, effective
  1 January 2027. The state describes it as making Illinois the first to require regular independent
  third-party safety audits of covered AI systems.
  Source (the Governor's own announcement):
  https://gov-pritzker-newsroom.prezly.com/gov-pritzker-signs-nation-leading-artificial-intelligence-safety-law

Because that category now exists, a reader could infer that we hold a place in it. We do not.

Council of AI is an independent measurement board. WE HOLD NO CERTIFICATION, DESIGNATION,
REGISTRATION OR ACCREDITATION UNDER ANY SUCH SCHEME — not in California, not in Illinois, not
anywhere — AND WE HAVE NEVER APPLIED FOR ONE. Nothing we publish is an AI audit required by any
statute, and nothing we publish should be filed as one. We measure, we sign, we publish the method
and the bank, and anyone can recompute it. Determination stays with authorities.

If that ever changes, this section changes with it and the change is recorded in the corrections
ledger at https://councilof.ai/api/corrections rather than quietly edited into these bytes.

## Same-site x402 offer and receipt checker
Download https://councilof.ai/verifier/verify_receipt.py; source-parity manifest https://councilof.ai/verifier/receipt-toolkit.json; dependency and offline-replay guide https://councilof.ai/verifier/receipt-toolkit.md. It is a separate format from card-v0 and GSPC cards. Signature verification is not settlement, freshness or measurement-truth verification. Default mode reads the public DID document; retained-key replay can be offline.
